2027-03-01.title: God Is Moving Behind The Scenes
2027-03-01.verse: After these things happened, the cupbearer to the king of Egypt and the royal baker offended their master, the king of Egypt. Pharaoh was enraged with his two officials, the cupbearer and the baker, so he imprisoned them in the house of the captain of the guard in the same facility where Joseph was confined. The captain of the guard appointed Joseph to be their attendant, and he served them. They spent some time in custody.
2027-03-01.observation: Some people have things come together and thank God. Then, when they realize just how much God moved, they become speechless. They realize that, while they were in the middle of their difficulty and complaining to God about all their hardships, God was moving and setting things into place that they did not notice at the time. Joseph does not realize it, but God was going to use events in Pharaoh's life to rescue him. It may have seemed like only a passing concern to Joseph at the moment. What does Pharaoh’s issue with a cupbearer have to do with his imprisonment? Many times we do not see how God connects the dots. It is only afterward that we realize God has been moving the entire time.
2027-03-01.application: Don’t try to connect the dots yourself. Just realize God is doing work you do not see now, but it will change everything later.
2027-03-01.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always being on the move in our lives.

2027-03-02.title: Wisdom Learned In Secret Will Show in Public
2027-03-02.verse: So Pharaoh asked his officials, “Can we find a man like Joseph, one in whom the Spirit of God is present?
2027-03-02.observation: In this chapter, Joseph is not only used by God to interpret the dream, he also stands out as having the wisdom to know how to save the nation. He has the skill to organize the relief effort and to plan out the long-term process of preparation. They were amazed at what he knew, but it does not appear they asked where he had learned it. They said the Lord had given it to him, but did they ever ask Joseph the vehicle or experiences God had led him through to learn it all? If they had, I wonder what they would have said when they learned that Joseph was taught by God through hidden suffering? Joseph learned preparation, administration, and patience by being a slave and being a prisoner. The skills we use are often taught to us in the storms of life. Therefore, do not despise seasons of “hiddenness.” God is teaching you how to thrive in other seasons.
2027-03-02.application: What are you learning in the current season you are in?
2027-03-02.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for never wasting a season. You use all things for the good of those who love You.

2027-03-03.title: When There Are No Good Choices
2027-03-03.verse: But Jacob replied, “My son will not go down there with you, for his brother is dead and he alone is left. If an accident happens to him on the journey you have to make, then you will bring down my gray hair in sorrow to the grave.
2027-03-03.observation: In today’s passage, Jacob has no good options. He cannot let his family starve, but he also feels he cannot let his youngest son go. What do you do when there are no good options? What do you do when it seems there is no way out? The only thing you can do is trust the Lord and make the next right decision. Jacob cannot see it now, so his son Reuben tries to talk with him. We must be willing to listen to those who love us and have our best interest at heart. Many times, all we can do is the best we can. The great secret is the Lord sees us and is already working in ways we do not yet realize. We think we are at the end of the story, but we are not even close. Soon, Jacob will be traveling to see a son he thought was dead. His willingness to make the next right choice, even though it was hard, will lead to an amazing miracle.
2027-03-03.application: What is the next right decision in your life?
2027-03-03.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for leading us when we do not realize it.

2027-03-04.title: God Will Lead You Out of Comfort Zones
2027-03-04.verse: Now the famine was severe in the land. When they finished eating the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Return, buy us a little more food.
2027-03-04.observation: We serve a God of miracles. A miracle is when God interrupts the natural order of the world He has made. Many times, He will do this to show Himself to us. In today’s passage, God could have performed a miracle so that the sons of Jacob did not need to go again to Egypt. However, God allowed natural law to continue in such a way that they were forced out of their comfort zone and confronted with a hard choice. They don’t know it yet, but this hard choice is going to lead them to healing their family wounds and it will ultimately save their family from the continually worsening famine. God could have worked a miracle, but He allowed natural order to continue for His purposes. The same is true today. We often pray and ask God to work miracles. When He does not do things the way we want, we may wonder why. Since God can do it, we should start wondering why He chose not to do it our way. Perhaps He is doing something else and leading us in ways we do not yet see. Maybe He is working to heal a wound we do not even realize we have.
2027-03-04.application: Where do you need to trust God’s leading today?
2027-03-04.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for leading us out of our comfort zones and into all You have for us.

2027-03-05.title: God is Working On Your Enemies, Too
2027-03-05.verse: Judah replied, “What can we say to my lord? What can we speak? How can we clear ourselves? God has exposed the sin of your servants! We are now my lord’s slaves, we and the one in whose possession the cup was found.
2027-03-05.observation: In this passage, we see that the brothers have finally learned the lesson they did not understand long ago. When Joseph was young, they despised their younger brother and were willing to sell him into slavery. Now, many years later, they are willing to take Benjamin’s place as slaves rather than see him become one. Many times, God will work in our lives and we will go through difficult seasons due to the actions of others. While that is happening, we can feel as though our enemies are locked in a pattern. We do not see them changing and going through their own struggles. This can cause us to wonder why God is sparing them from the same pain we endure. However, God is not silent or deaf to the situations in our lives. Just like the Lord was working in Joseph and his brothers’ lives, God works on us and our enemies at the same time. Therefore, do not worry about what God is doing in them. Trust He is leading and molding them, just like He is you.
2027-03-05.application: Who do you need to let go and trust God with today?
2027-03-05.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always doing more than we can see.

2027-03-06.title: Goodness Brings Favor
2027-03-06.verse: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals and go to the land of Canaan! Get your father and your households and come to me! Then I will give you the best land in Egypt and you will eat the best of the land.’
2027-03-06.observation: One of the aspects of the story of Joseph is the kindness shown to him by the pharaoh. This is a stark contrast to what we will find in the book of Exodus. This pharaoh likely had great respect for Joseph because he was used by God to organize a relief effort before they even knew they needed it. According to the text, it appears as though Joseph showed integrity in all his preparations and continued to do his job, even after being vindicated. Therefore, when it was time for Joseph to need something, pharaoh went overboard in being gracious. We should never be good in order to manipulate people. However, being good has its rewards. When we show goodness to others, the Lord has a way of returning it to us in ways we do not always expect.
2027-03-06.application: Who is someone that has shown you kindness that now needs your help today?
2027-03-06.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being the ultimate Good in our lives.

2027-03-07.title: God Walks With Us To The End
2027-03-07.verse: He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there. I will go down with you to Egypt and I myself will certainly bring you back from there. Joseph will close your eyes.
2027-03-07.observation: While the Bible does not say this specifically, it’s possible to wonder if Jacob thought he could have been leaving God behind. During this time in history, many people believed there were gods everywhere and they all occupied certain geographical regions. This is another reason why it was such a big deal for Abraham to leave everything and go to an unknown land. In his mind, it could have been truly stepping out into a vulnerable place. It is possible that God is reminding Jacob that He is not bound by a certain place. He will not leave Jacob as he goes into a new area. God will go with Jacob and be with him even to the point of death. This is a great reminder for us. God is not bound by space and time. There is nowhere we can go that He does not go with us. He is there. He will continue to walk with us. He goes with us through it all, all the way to the end and beyond.
2027-03-07.application: How would your day change if you realized there is nowhere you will go that God will not go, too?
2027-03-07.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for walking with us through every season and situation of life.

2027-03-08.title: Prospering in Problem Times
2027-03-08.verse: Israel settled in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen, and they owned land there. They were fruitful and increased rapidly in number.
2027-03-08.observation: While the nation of Egypt was suffering and slowly losing everything into the hands of Pharaoh, the Lord was blessing the nation of Israel as they settled into their new home. This is not the home they wanted, but they were making the best of it. When they decided to go “all in” and trust the Lord was leading them, it turned out better than they probably hoped it would. When we decide we will embrace the change God has brought us to, we can find a new momentum we didn’t expect. This does not always mean we will prosper on the outside. There will be difficult seasons that God will allow into our lives for different reasons. However, He always goes with us and our soul prospers as we know He will take care of us through it all.
2027-03-08.application: How can your soul prosper during the current season you are experiencing?
2027-03-08.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for taking difficult seasons and turning them into fertilizer for future growth.

2027-03-09.title: The Lord is With Us, Not Just Our Heroes
2027-03-09.verse: Then Israel said to Joseph, “I am about to die, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers.
2027-03-09.observation: Many times, we hear of the amazing feats of our heroes in the faith and almost think they have a different relationship with God than we do. God is the same, but it seems like they have attained a place in Him that simply is not possible for us. This is, of course, not true. Jacob is reminding Joseph that God will be with Joseph the same way He has been with him. It’s important that we realize God does not have any favorites in His kingdom. He loves us all. What God does in someone’s life has nothing to do with how He feels about us. If nothing else, it is a blessing. We can look at what God has done through someone else and realize that same God loves us, too.
2027-03-09.application: Never look at someone else to determine if God loves you. He does love you and it is more than you can imagine.
2027-03-09.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for loving us all with an everlasting love.

2027-03-10.title: God Gives Us What We Need
2027-03-10.verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel. This is what their father said to them when he blessed them. He gave each of them an appropriate blessing.
2027-03-10.observation: If you have had brothers or sisters, you possibly have the same thought I had when reading this chapter. I wonder if any of these brothers were listening to what their father said and gauged it by what he said about them. There is something about us humans that we are constantly comparing ourselves to each other. There is a great moment in a book I read once about a magic mirror that would show you your deepest heart’s desire. The author of the book said that the “well-ordered mind” would look back at the mirror and see only a reflection of themselves. In other words, they had made peace with themselves and did not need to be anyone else. I would say this is also the attribute of the mature Christian. We realize that God does not consult our neighbor to determine His plan for our lives. He blesses us according to what He has in store for us. Therefore, we can rejoice with our neighbor because God loves us both and each of us stands on our own before the Lord with joy.
2027-03-10.application: Take joy in knowing God loves you without regard for your neighbor, their successes, and failures.
2027-03-10.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for loving us the way You do.

2027-03-11.title: All Things Work Together for Good
2027-03-11.verse: But Joseph answered them, “Don’t be afraid. Am I in the place of God? As for you, you meant to harm me, but God intended it for a good purpose, so he could preserve the lives of many people, as you can see this day. So now, don’t be afraid. I will provide for you and your little children.” Then he consoled them and spoke kindly to them.
2027-03-11.observation: Many of us would not have a problem with Joseph if he were bitter with his brothers. It was their act that sent him to Egypt. However, Joseph has a different point of view. He sees God at work in every one of his difficulties. He realized that God used all the events of his life as vehicles to get him to the place he currently enjoyed. This did not absolve his brothers of justice. He reminded them that God alone was going to do the punishing. However, Joseph was not going to allow what they did to keep him from seeing the good. When we begin to realize that no one can stop God from doing what He wants to do in our lives, we begin to stop seeing people as having the power to stop us. We see everything as part of God’s ultimate plan.
2027-03-11.application: How would it change your day if you realized that all things will be used by God for your good?
2027-03-11.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being trustworthy. We trust that You never waste anything we go through.

2027-03-12.title: Jesus Reigns
2027-03-12.verse: This is the record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
2027-03-12.observation: Matthew was written to the Jewish people, but for us all. Matthew spends the first chapter proving that Jesus had a claim to the physical throne of Israel by proving His authentic lineage. Then, Matthew spends the rest of his Gospel showing that Jesus is so much more than an earthly king. He is the King of kings. The Jewish nation was expecting an earthly king to come and raise an army to defeat the Romans. When Jesus came, they did not know what to do with Him because He was altogether different. This is because He did not come to conquer the Roman government. He came to do so much more.
2027-03-12.application: Take time to think about how the plan of God was so much bigger than setting one nation free from governmental oppression. He came to free all of humanity.
2027-03-12.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for having much bigger plans than we can imagine.

2027-03-13.title: To See But Not to Perceive
2027-03-13.verse: After assembling all the chief priests and experts in the law, he asked them where the Christ was to be born. “In Bethlehem of Judea,” they said, “for it is written this way by the prophet:
2027-03-13.observation: It blows my mind to think that when asked, the scribes knew exactly where Jesus was born. They had been waiting on this day for a long time. Think about it. Out of nowhere, these people come and say they have traveled across the known world to see the new king. When asked, the scribes told them the exact town to go to. However, the Bible does not speak of any scribes who saddled up a camel and followed. Were they not even a little curious? It might have been because they did not think the Messiah could be born without their knowledge. They could see the Scriptures, but could not perceive them being fulfilled in any other way than their expectations. We should also approach God’s Word with humility and realize that we do not know how God will fulfill His prophecies. We trust Him to do what only He can do. That’s enough.
2027-03-13.application: When reading God’s Word, apply clear interpretation guidelines. One guideline when approaching prophecy is humility. We do not know it all.
2027-03-13.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always being greater than us.

2027-03-14.title: Prove It
2027-03-14.verse: Therefore produce fruit that proves your repentance,
2027-03-14.observation: One of my favorite phrases is, “prove it.” I love using this when talking to someone who has a smug air about them and claims to know something about God’s Word that is clearly not there. However, this is a double-edged sword. People have also used this phrase against me, and it was humbling. The point John the Baptist is making is that talk is cheap. Have proof for what you say or proclaim. We need to have proof for our claim to be Christians. If we are Christians, it should show by how we live more than what we proclaim. No one should ever have to ask us to prove it. We should be proving it every day in how we live. Out of the joy of our salvation, we should pursue God in our everyday lives. By this, the byproduct will be the fruit of the Spirit or the “proof” of our pursuit of God.
2027-03-14.application: Prove what you proclaim by how you live.
2027-03-14.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for working on us while we work to walk toward You.

2027-03-16.title: The Scripture Has Power
2027-03-16.observation: While Jesus was on Earth in physical form, He had all the power of God living in Him. He could have called all the armies of Heaven at any point, but He walked in humble submission to show us the way. This passage could be seen as a pro NBA player playing one-on-one with a 5-year-old kid. It is not even close to a fair game. The NBA player would easily defeat the child and maybe even have a hard time using it as a training lesson for others because there would be such a disparity of skill. That is a way to see this interaction between Jesus and the devil. He is not struggling with the devil. He is teaching us. When we are confronted with temptation, we remember God’s Word. If something would cause us to violate God’s Word, we see it for what it is and move on. If it lines up with the freedom found in God’s Word, we step forward. God’s Word is here to help us know Him and enjoy Him forever. We should never see it as a burden. It is the key to lasting joy.
2027-03-16.application: Memorize a promise from God’s Word that speaks against the greatest temptation in your life. When temptation comes, quote God’s Word to yourself out loud. Watch what happens.
2027-03-16.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for showing us the way.

2027-03-17.title: Peace Workers, Not Peace Keepers
2027-03-17.verse: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called the children of God.
2027-03-17.observation: There is a difference between keeping the peace and working for peace. Keeping the peace is something you do after you have made peace. Making peace often requires seasons of organized chaos. It involves challenging things and creating tension. The goal is to set things in order, then keep it that way. In ancient times, when a king wanted to create a wider peace, he would do so by declaring war on the surrounding nations. He knew that peace only came through the resolution of ongoing conflict. To make this happen, he would need to resolve the conflict. Then, peace could reign.
2027-03-17.application: Where do you need to “declare war” and find healthy resolution so you can bring peace?
2027-03-17.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for giving us the courage to work toward peace.

2027-03-18.title: Why Pray?
2027-03-18.verse: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
2027-03-18.observation: Have you ever wondered why we pray? This verse takes it a step further because God already knows what we are going to pray. So, why pray? There are many reasons we should pray. The first and most obvious reason to pray is that God’s Word commands us to pray. That is enough. However, there is another reason. We pray in order to fellowship with the Lord. We pray to spend time with the Lord and enjoy being with our Heavenly Father. Recently, one of my daughters came into my study and just sat with me. We did not really cover a lot of information. We just spent time in each other’s presence. It was refreshing just to be near someone I love that much. It’s like that with God. Be careful not to think of prayer as an overly formal, agenda-laden meeting. It is fellowship with your Heavenly Father.
2027-03-18.application: Set aside time to sit in prayer and simply share what is on your mind.
2027-03-18.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for caring about simply spending time with us.

2027-03-19.title: Don’t Sit In Judgment
2027-03-19.verse: Do not judge so that you will not be judged. For by the standard you judge you will be judged, and the measure you use will be the measure you receive.
2027-03-19.observation: This verse has stopped many conversations that could have been helpful. We will never know. While some people have used this Scripture to stop people from engaging in unhealthy conversations, the majority of people use this Scripture to stop someone from saying something we do not like. Is that what Jesus is saying? Is He saying we should never disagree with anyone or challenge someone we love if we see something possibly harmful in their life? No. This cannot be what Jesus is saying because just a few verses later He talks about knowing a tree because of the fruit it produces. That would mean we are “judging” a tree to be an apple tree if we see it is producing apples. What does Jesus mean? If we read the context, we realize He is saying we should not sit in a “seat of judgment” against someone. Let God decide what is just and unjust punishment for what someone does. There is a difference between saying someone is lying and saying you are going to slap someone because they are lying. Let God cast the judgment for their sin. We can mark someone by how they live. Now, what do we do with what we judge? Jesus also talks about that. He says we should focus on getting the “log” out of our own eye before we presume to tell someone with a “speck” how to get their life right.
2027-03-19.application: Is there someone that you have been afraid to talk to because you have misinterpreted this verse? How do you need to pray for the Lord to open the door of conversation? How will you approach them in a healthy way?
2027-03-19.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for giving us the wisdom to see and the patience to watch You work.

2027-03-20.title: Jesus is Willing
2027-03-20.verse: He stretched out his hand and touched him saying, “I am willing. Be clean!” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
2027-03-20.observation: This is one of my favorite stories in all of Matthew. This leper had lost everything, including his hope for the future. He is face to face with Jesus. This is also a massive gamble because he is not supposed to be close to anyone. Leprosy was a death sentence. With his last remaining hope, he is not demanding anything of Jesus. He is acknowledging Jesus’ ability and is asking for His willingness. This is both faith and request. Jesus’ response? He says, “Of course I am willing to heal you.” What would it look like for us to approach God with this kind of humility? It reminds me of the story of the three Hebrew teenagers in the book of Daniel. When threatened with being thrown into a fire for not worshiping idols, they said that God was able to save them. However, even if He did not do it, they would still not serve the idols. This is powerful faith that God rewards with His favor.
2027-03-20.application: During your prayer time today, have the posture of the man in this story. God is able to do anything. Pray and ask if He is willing to do it your way. Remember to confess that you will still serve Him either way. Watch how it lightens your heart as you realize no matter what happens, God is in control.
2027-03-20.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for having it all in Your powerful hands.

2027-03-21.title: The Greatest Miracle
2027-03-21.verse: When Jesus perceived their thoughts he said, “Why do you respond with evil in your hearts? Which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven’ or to say, ‘Stand up and walk’? But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he said to the paralytic—“Stand up, take your stretcher, and go home.
2027-03-21.observation: Jesus shows infinite kindness to the paralyzed man, giving him the greatest miracle first. Those around did not see Jesus as God, so they thought it was impossible for Jesus to absolve this man of his sin. Jesus shows us all that forgiving sin and healing a sickness is impossible for us, but both are possible for Him. We can have confidence that, even if we cannot see it the way we might see a physical healing, our sins can be forgiven. Jesus gave this man the greatest gift first. He was free from his sin. Then, He healed his body as well. Never forget that your salvation is just as much a miracle as watching someone paralyzed getting up and walking. It is the greatest miracle.
2027-03-21.application: Think of yourself as someone who has received a healing that would shock the world around you. It’s true. You have received salvation.
2027-03-21.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for giving us the greatest miracle we could receive when You gave us Your salvation.

2027-03-22.title: Take Your Brain With You
2027-03-22.verse: I am sending you out like sheep surrounded by wolves, so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.
2027-03-22.observation: In this passage, Jesus tells us two truths that can be powerful if we will listen. First, He tells us that people are not nice by nature. We are born into a fallen world due to the sin of Adam and Eve. Romans says all have turned away and there are none who are righteous. Jeremiah says the heart is deceitfully wicked. Therefore, we should live expecting people without God to act like people who are not living with Kingdom ethics. The second truth is be wise. I have known of many well-meaning Christians who say things like, “I’m going to move forward and the Lord will be with me.” That is true, but they use it as a way of saying they can wade into a metaphorical wolf pack and not get bitten simply because they are a Christian. Jesus says one of the gifts He gave us is the ability to be shrewd or wise. He expects us to use the good brain He gave us. Then, if bad things come, He will still be with us. So, the bottom line is to have a plan and expect difficulty.
2027-03-22.application: What does it do for you to realize bad things will happen because we live in a bad world? That means it may have nothing to do with you. You’re not evil. You’re not “deserving.” Jesus came to save us from all this.
2027-03-22.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for revealing to us the rules of the road.

2027-03-23.title: Come to Jesus
2027-03-23.verse: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke on you and learn from me because I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy to bear, and my load is not hard to carry.
2027-03-23.observation: When growing up, I thought this verse meant that coming to Jesus was a step toward getting rid of all our responsibilities. I thought bringing my burdens to Jesus meant that He would carry them for me. There was even a popular song that said, “Take your burdens to the Lord and leave it there.” This is a powerful way to think about prayer and we should allow God to carry heavy burdens. However, this verse means something even greater. Jesus is showing a word-picture of someone coming to Him with the heaviness of life. Jesus, as the Master Carpenter, fits a yoke that can evenly carry the weight. The most common yoke was for a pair of oxen. They were custom made to fit the oxen so they were able to carry heavy loads without becoming injured. He is saying when we come to Him, He will carry it with us and teach us to carry the responsibilities of life without injury.
2027-03-23.application: Have you ever thought about how God takes away some of your difficulties and how He walks with you through others? This is not God missing some of your issues. What if it is Him teaching us how to carry loads with Him? He is always there.
2027-03-23.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always walking with us.

2027-03-24.title: God’s Family
2027-03-24.verse: And pointing toward his disciples he said, “Here are my mother and my brothers! For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
2027-03-24.observation: Jesus is making a powerful statement that the Kingdom of God is not made up of insiders and outsiders. All are welcome. All can become an insider if they are willing to bow to the Lordship of Christ. He leads and we follow. When we do this, it is called salvation. We exchange our sin for His sacrifice on the Cross. This provides our salvation. We are then invited into His family, not as slaves, but as sons and daughters. Jesus is reminding the crowd that His family is made up of those who follow Him. If you are a Christ-follower, you are now part of the Kingdom of God. Elsewhere in the New Testament, it is likened to a wild branch being grafted into an olive tree. We are now part of the family of God.
2027-03-24.application: Have you ever thought about this meaning the people in the Bible are your adopted family? You’re related, by salvation, to King David and Moses. We are all part of God’s Heavenly family.
2027-03-24.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for accepting us into Your family.

2027-03-25.title: When We Discover the Kingdom
2027-03-25.verse: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure, hidden in a field, that a person found and hid. Then because of joy he went and sold all that he had and bought that field. “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant searching for fine pearls. When he found a pearl of great value, he went out and sold everything he had and bought it.
2027-03-25.observation: I love this analogy. Jesus is using a parable, or story, to explain a complex spiritual principle. In this story, He speaks of someone on the lookout for what he needs. As a merchant, he would be looking for things of value to be sold. He finds the greatest prize he could hope to discover. This prize is not for sale. He becomes the buyer. He changes his entire goal in life and is now satisfied with what he has discovered. Jesus is saying the Kingdom of Heaven is like that. People spend their whole lives looking for something. Some people are looking for love, some are looking for meaning, and some are looking for security for the future. Jesus says that when we discover the Kingdom of Heaven and His goodness, we become the chaser. We dive in and never look back.
2027-03-25.application: When is the last time you thought of being a Christian as a lifelong adventure with God? You have discovered the greatest miracle. Celebrate that today.
2027-03-25.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, that it was really You who found us.

2027-03-26.title: I Am Here
2027-03-26.verse: But immediately Jesus spoke to them: “Have courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.
2027-03-26.observation: I recently heard a statement that says, “Confidence comes from competence.” There is a lot of truth in this. If you want real confidence, go out and gather data to back up your claim by learning and growing. Find evidence to back up what you want to proclaim. The disciples had walked with Jesus. Even though they were astonished to see Jesus walking on water, He was the only one who could have been expected to do such a thing. The Source of our confidence is that the only God is here with us. He does not always keep us out of danger, but He walks with us into each of them. Therefore, our confidence in any storm does not come from our own ability. It comes from the “data we have collected.” We have witnessed the Lord overcome time and time again. He is here and He brings His glory with Him. All is well.
2027-03-26.application: Remind yourself throughout your day that the Lord is with you.
2027-03-26.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being with us in all things.

2027-03-27.title: Our Faith Brings Us to God
2027-03-27.verse: Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, your faith is great! Let what you want be done for you.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.
2027-03-27.observation: Throughout the Scriptures, we see Jesus saying over and over that someone’s faith is what healed them. I have heard some people say that means that our faith is some sort of powerful muscle that is part of the healing. They say this to imply that we have some type of power separate from God. Jesus says this over and over again because it takes faith to bring something to God. For example, in this passage, this lady had to have great faith to come to Jesus, make it through the difficulty of the disciples, and make it past some initial pushback from Jesus. It is our willingness to come to God with all we have and not stop trusting Him that Jesus applauds. If God were to take a love language test, the greatest way to show Him love is through trust.
2027-03-27.application: Trust the Lord, today, in all things. When you face a challenge, have the faith to bring it to God and trust that He will not leave you in it.
2027-03-27.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always walking with us and rewarding our faith with Your presence.

2027-03-28.title: The Price of Life
2027-03-28.verse: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone wants to become my follower, he must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
2027-03-28.observation: I have heard it said many times that salvation is free, and it is. However, we need to break this down a little for clarity. First of all, salvation was not free for Jesus. It cost Jesus the suffering of the Cross, death by the Romans, and Resurrection. Our salvation was actually very expensive. It is free for us to receive because Jesus paid so high a cost. The next aspect to be considered is that many think that ends the story. Salvation is free, but it also comes with a promise on our end. We say to God, “I receive Your salvation and will now follow You.” Jesus says in the passage today that the cost of salvation is living our lives for Him. By taking up our cross, Jesus means we follow Him without looking back. For some, that may sound like false advertisement. They may say, “When someone told me about salvation, they told me that Jesus wanted to wash away my sins. That’s all. I did not realize I had to live for Him, too.” That’s a feature, not a bug. With the Lord comes all His goodness, mercy, and kindness. The One who loves you the most desires to now lead you into all life. Jesus did not come to take away our lives, but to give us true life. Instead of saying, “I have to follow Him, too,” our response should be, “You mean I get to follow Him too?!”
2027-03-28.application: Celebrate the reality that God does not just want to save you, He wants to do life with you.
2027-03-28.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for wanting to be a part of all of our lives.

2027-03-29.title: A Glimpse of Glory
2027-03-29.verse: And he was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as light. Then Moses and Elijah also appeared before them, talking with him.
2027-03-29.observation: I wonder if it was possible to get used to seeing Jesus every day. They would see amazing things so much that it might have been possible to develop a kind of apathy toward the miraculous. This day probably set everyone straight. Without knowing it was coming, Jesus let the “veil” slip a little and allowed His body to transform into a glorified state. I wonder if this is why Peter was so adamant that he would go with Jesus to the death. After seeing Jesus in a moment of His glory, he could not unsee this majesty. Peter is still talking about it when he tells the story to Mark so that it eventually becomes part of that Gospel. He’s even talking about it years later when he writes what we call 2 Peter. A moment of God’s glory marked him for life. This can be the same for us. A moment of glory can change it all.
2027-03-29.application: Spend time in God’s presence and focus on worshiping God. See God for who He is, not just all He has done. He is the King of kings and the Lord of lords. Then, carry that with you throughout the day.
2027-03-29.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, our King, for being a glorious King.

2027-03-31.title: God is There
2027-03-31.verse: For where two or three are assembled in my name, I am there among them.
2027-03-31.observation: God is omnipresent. This means God stands outside of all things, but all things exist within Him. This means there is no place where God is not also present. While that can be a difficult concept to get our minds to comprehend, the bottom line is the same. There is nowhere that God is not present. This is helpful, because we can sometimes feel as though God is far away. This is not possible. So, no matter where you are and no matter who is with you, God is also there.
2027-03-31.application: Take time to think about God always being close in all seasons of life.
2027-03-31.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for never letting us walk through a moment alone.
